name: Albania

facts.religion: Muslim about 50% (Sunni and Bektashi), Catholic and Orthodox Christian, many non-practising

snapshot: Edi Rama won a fourth term in 2025, but in October 2026 student-led protests over corruption turned violent and spread from Tirana to other cities.
culture: Under Enver Hoxha, Albania became the world's first officially atheist state and the most isolated country in Europe, leaving hundreds of thousands of concrete bunkers. Today Muslims, Catholics and Orthodox Christians live side by side with little friction. Iso-polyphony, a form of folk singing, is UNESCO-listed, and the besa, a code of honour, is part of national identity.
society: Around a third of Albanians live abroad, mainly in Italy, Greece and Britain. Tourism along the Riviera has boomed, as have property and cannabis-linked money laundering. Rama has appointed an AI-generated "minister" to oversee public procurement as an anti-corruption gimmick. Organised crime groups have reach across Europe.
situation: Edi Rama's Socialist Party won a fourth consecutive term in May 2025 with a large majority, and Albania aims to finish EU accession talks by 2027. In 2026 the mood soured: summer protests against a luxury coastal development backed by Jared Kushner gave way in October to student-led demonstrations over corruption, jobs and schools, in which government buildings and banks were set on fire and hundreds of people were charged. Rama refused to resign, calling the protests a threat to EU membership rather than to his government.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the 140-seat Assembly; the president is elected by parliament and largely ceremonial.
